Fit a Negative Binomial GLMM for overdispersed wait-time analysis

Source: R/nb_model.R
mysterycall_nb_model.Rd

Runs a multilevel negative binomial regression (glmmTMB::glmmTMB) for mystery caller studies where the Poisson model shows overdispersion (mysterycall_poisson_model() reports phi > 2). The physician identifier is modelled as a random intercept. Fixed-effect results are returned as incidence rate ratios (IRR) with Wald confidence intervals.

Usage

mysterycall_nb_model(
  data,
  outcome,
  predictors,
  random_intercept,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  offset_col = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing all model columns. Rows with NA in any model column are dropped before fitting.

outcome

Character scalar naming the count-outcome column (e.g. "business_days_until_appointment"). Must be non-negative integer-valued.

predictors

Character vector of fixed-effect predictor column names. Factor and character columns are used as-is; the reference level is the first level alphabetically (or the first levels() for factors).

random_intercept

Character scalar naming the grouping column for the random intercept (e.g. "npi" for physician). A (1 | column) term is added to the formula automatically.

conf_level

Confidence level for Wald CIs. Default 0.95.

offset_col

Optional character scalar naming a numeric column to use as a log-offset. When supplied, offset(log(offset_col)) is appended to the fixed-effects formula.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to glmmTMB::glmmTMB().

Value

A list of class mysterycall_nb_model containing:

model

glmmTMB. The fitted model object.

irr_table

tibble. One row per fixed-effect term: term, estimate (log scale), se, z_value, p_value, p_value_fmt, irr, ci_lower, ci_upper.

theta

numeric. Negative binomial dispersion parameter (shape, theta > 0). Higher values indicate less overdispersion. Variance = mean + mean^2 / theta.

random_effects

data.frame from lme4::VarCorr().

factor_refs

list. Reference levels for character/factor predictors.

formula

formula. The formula passed to glmmTMB.

n

integer. Complete-case rows used.

n_dropped

integer. Rows excluded for missing values.

n_clusters

integer. Unique values of random_intercept.

overdispersion

numeric. Pearson chi-square / residual df after NB fit. Values near 1 indicate adequate fit. Values > 2 suggest the NB model still underfits; consider zero-inflated NB.

convergence

list. converged (logical), messages (character vector).

aic

numeric. AIC.

bic

numeric. BIC.

Details

Use this function when mysterycall_poisson_model() returns overdispersion substantially greater than 2: the negative binomial adds a per-observation variance term (theta) that absorbs the excess variance and yields correctly-sized standard errors.

When to use negative binomial vs Poisson

Run mysterycall_poisson_model() first. If result$overdispersion > 2, switch to mysterycall_nb_model(). The negative binomial model will give wider (more honest) confidence intervals and correct p-values; Poisson standard errors are deflated under overdispersion, producing spuriously small p-values.

Interpreting theta

theta (the shape parameter) controls how quickly variance grows with the mean. As theta -> Inf, the NB distribution approaches Poisson. Values of theta < 5 indicate substantial overdispersion.

See also

mysterycall_poisson_model() for the Poisson equivalent; mysterycall_wait_time_summary() for descriptive summaries.

Examples

set.seed(1978)
df <- data.frame(
  wait_days = rnbinom(40, mu = 18, size = 2),
  insurance = rep(c("Medicaid", "BCBS"), each = 20),
  gender    = sample(c("Male", "Female"), 40, replace = TRUE),
  physician = rep(paste0("Dr_", 1:8), each = 5),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
result <- mysterycall_nb_model(
  df,
  outcome          = "wait_days",
  predictors       = c("insurance", "gender"),
  random_intercept = "physician"
)
#> Fitting Negative Binomial GLMM: wait_days ~ insurance + gender + (1 | physician)
#> Model fitted: n=40, physicians=8, AIC=299.0, theta=1.99
result$irr_table
